domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2.
s has exactly n minus 1 entries.
Each entry s_i is restricted to the two values plus 1 and minus 1.
V(s) is a subset of the indices from 1 to n.
The valley condition at j is only defined for interior indices j from 2 to n minus 1.
The adjacent product conclusion only ranges over i from 1 to n minus 2.
Odd and even integers are interpreted relative to the set of integers from 1 to n.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n at least 2 and every length n minus 1 sign sequence with entries plus 1 or minus 1, the valley set definition has the following rigidity property: if V(s) is exactly the odd indices, then the sequence alternates starting with plus 1; if V(s) is exactly the even indices, then the sequence alternates starting with minus 1; equivalently, whenever V(s) is exactly one parity class, consecutive entries of the sequence always have opposite signs.
quantifier_order: For every integer n with n at least 2.
For every sign sequence s of length n minus 1 with each entry equal to plus 1 or minus 1.
If the valley set V(s) is exactly the odd indices in the range from 1 to n, then every entry s_i is plus 1 for odd i and minus 1 for even i.
If the valley set V(s) is exactly the even indices in the range from 1 to n, then every entry s_i is minus 1 for odd i and plus 1 for even i.
Equivalently, if V(s) is exactly one parity class, then for every i from 1 to n minus 2, the adjacent entries satisfy s_i times s_{i+1} equals minus 1.

statement_nl: Let n be an integer with n at least 2, and let s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) be a sign sequence with each s_i equal to plus 1 or minus 1. Define the valley set V(s) subset of {1,...,n} by: 1 belongs to V(s) exactly when s_1 = plus 1; n belongs to V(s) exactly when s_{n-1} = minus 1; and for 2 <= j <= n-1, j belongs to V(s) exactly when s_{j-1} = minus 1 and s_j = plus 1. If V(s) is exactly the set of odd integers in {1,...,n}, then s_i = plus 1 for odd i and s_i = minus 1 for even i. If V(s) is exactly the set of even integers in {1,...,n}, then s_i = minus 1 for odd i and s_i = plus 1 for even i. Equivalently, if V(s) is a full parity class, then s_i s_{i+1} = -1 for every i=1,...,n-2.
